label: prf:calibration-cohomology-alignment
title: Proof of the calibration–cohomology alignment
html:
The count. H^1(\text{Bring}) = 2W is a polarised weight-1 Hodge structure. The W-isotypic part is the tensor W \otimes \mathbb{C}^2, with the \mathbb{C}^2 the Hodge multiplicity plane (H^{1,0} \oplus H^{0,1}). A polarised rank-2 weight-1 Hodge structure has two real moduli — an overall scale and a modulus (period ratio) — and these are the only invariants of the S_5-equivariant Gauss--Manin data on that plane (the equivariance forces M = \mathrm{id}_W \otimes B, so all freedom lives in the 2\times 2 block B: its normalisation and its \mathrm{SL}_2 trace \tau, since \det B = 1). That is 2 data. The meson topology is the Hopf link, whose complement has \mathrm{Vol} = 0 (meson scale-independence); it carries no hyperbolic-volume invariant, so its mass scale is a third datum independent of (m_e, q_0). Total 2 + 1 = 3 (cohomology_data_count).

The alignment. The scale of the W-plane is the n=0 period a_D^{(e)} = m_e (CAL-1, prop:electron-period-base); its modulus is \tau, fixed by q_0 (CAL-2, prop:sl2-prolongation-recurrence); the meson-sector scale is m_\pi (CAL-3). The calibration triple (m_e, q_0\text{-modulus}, m_\pi) therefore equals the cohomological triple (\text{scale}, \text{modulus}, \text{meson scale}) term by term (QOU.Mass.calibrations_eq_cohomology). \qquad\blacksquare
